A host read of the indented region shows leading whitespace matching the configured indentation width and kind on every affected line.
A host read of the rectangularly edited file shows the typed text once on each selected line and on no other line.

recovery_cases.description: If undo splits or merges a compound edit differently from the recorded transaction boundaries, the divergence is recorded as a defect rather than accepted as equivalent.
A file whose encoding the product does not support is reported as unsupported and is not silently rewritten; the host bytes stay identical.
Toggling wrapping back off restores the previous viewport and leaves the buffer text and the caret offset unchanged.
Clearing the extra cursor leaves a single caret and no orphan insertion point; a stray cursor that keeps receiving input fails the run.
Move OS focus away mid-selection and back; the selection, the cursor set and the undo stack survive and the next edit applies to the same buffer.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the three prepared files before and after, their host byte dumps, the recorded intermediate buffer states and the diagnostics list. All content is synthetic fixture text created for the run. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, open a fixture file whose bytes are recorded from the host, and enable Vim modal editing through the ordinary setting.
Confirm the product reports normal mode and that the mode indicator is visible.
Type a sequence of normal-mode motion keys and, after each, record the reported cursor position and confirm no motion key was inserted into the buffer.
Apply an operator over a motion, for example delete to end of word and change inside a bracket pair, and confirm the buffer changes exactly as the operator describes.
Yank a range into a named register, move the caret, and put it back at the new position, confirming the text appears at the target and that the source is left as the operator defines.
Overwrite the same register with a second yank and put again, confirming the register holds the most recent content.
Enter insert mode explicitly, type text, leave insert mode, and confirm the typed text was inserted once and that the key which entered insert mode was not itself inserted.
Move OS focus to another application and back, then repeat one operator and confirm it still applies to the authoritative buffer.
Save the file and read it from the host, comparing the bytes against the recorded sequence of operations.
Disable Vim mode and confirm ordinary typing resumes with no leftover modal interception.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the saved file shows exactly the text the recorded operator, register and insert operations describe, with no stray normal-mode character present.

A host diff between the recorded pre-run bytes and the saved bytes contains no occurrence of the normal-mode command characters used in the run other than where they were deliberately typed in insert mode.
A platform accessibility dump reports the focused text element caret offset after each motion, and it matches the position the product reported.
The OS reports the product process id unchanged across the whole sequence, so no crash and restart masked a lost or duplicated key.

recovery_cases.description: A normal-mode key sequence the product does not implement is reported as unhandled; it is neither inserted as text nor silently dropped.
After a focus change the mode indicator still reports the mode that was active, and the first key after return is interpreted in that mode.
Putting from an empty register reports an empty register and inserts nothing.
Disabling Vim mode mid-session leaves the buffer intact and the next keystroke inserts text normally.
If Vim modal editing cannot be enabled in the packaged build, the run records failed with the exact missing setting and is never recorded as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the fixture file before and after, the recorded key sequence with its reported caret positions, and the accessibility dump filtered to the Legion window subtree. No OS-wide key log is captured or retained. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Generate a 100 MB text fixture with a known line count and content markers into a disposable directory from a host shell, and record its size and SHA-256.
Launch the packaged product with a host clock running, open the fixture, and record the interval between the open request and the first rendered content.
Record the state the product reports for the buffer and confirm it names one of the declared full, degraded or streaming states rather than an unlabelled condition.
Confirm the streaming or degraded state is visible in the UI with a plain-language explanation of what is reduced.
Scroll from the start of the file to the end and back, sampling the rendered content against the known markers at several recorded offsets.
While scrolling continues, type a unique marker into the buffer and measure the interval between the keystroke and the character being painted using the host clock or a high-frame-rate capture.
Repeat the input-to-paint measurement in a small ordinary file for comparison, and record both figures against the declared budget.
Open a second ordinary file in another tab while the large file stays open, and confirm ordinary editing there is unaffected.
Save the large file if the reported state permits it, or record the refusal, then read the file from the host and compare its size and marker positions with the recorded values.

external_oracles.description: A host clock or a high-frame-rate screen capture measures the open time and the input-to-paint intervals independently of any figure the product reports.
A host read of the fixture at the sampled offsets returns the same content the product rendered at those offsets.
A host stat of the fixture after the session shows the expected size and, if a save occurred, the typed marker as the only change.
A host process sampler records the product's resident memory and CPU during the open and the scroll, so a claimed streaming mode is distinguishable from a full in-memory load.

recovery_cases.description: An open or input-to-paint measurement outside the declared budget is recorded as a failed budget with the measured figure, never rounded or repeated until favourable.
A buffer state the product cannot name as full, degraded or streaming is recorded as a defect.
If the reported state refuses a save, the refusal is explicit and the on-disk file is unchanged.
If the product exhausts memory or exits, the host records the exit and the run is failed; the fixture on disk must still be intact.

If no host clock or capture facility can measure input-to-paint on this configuration, the timing part of the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite rather than taken from the product's own report.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the fixture metadata, the recorded timing measurements, the host resource samples and the sampled marker comparisons. The fixture is synthetic generated content; no user file is used. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone with a workspace shell profile configured that differs from the platform default, and record both from a host shell.

Open the terminal panel, confirm the shell the product reports is the configured workspace profile rather than the platform default, and record the child process image path from a host process listing.

Set a policy-denied environment variable and a secret-shaped variable in the host environment before launch, then inspect the spawned child's environment from the host and confirm neither value is present.
Run the project's test command, for example `cargo test` in the Rust fixture, let it complete, and record the reported exit status, working directory and per-command boundaries.

Compare the reported working directory and exit status with the values a host shell obtains for the same command, and confirm the OSC 133 command boundaries and OSC 7 directory updates the product parsed match the shell's actual behavior.
Produce output containing a URL and more lines than the configured scrollback bound; confirm link detection, scroll back to the oldest retained line, and search the output for a known marker.
Select a region of output, copy it, and read the OS clipboard from the host to confirm the copied text matches the selection and carries no appended metadata.
Open a second terminal session, run a different command in it, and switch between the two sessions confirming each keeps its own output view, running state and exit status.

Resize the panel while a program is running and confirm the child observes the new size, then kill the child from the host and confirm the session reports crashed or exited truthfully and offers restart or reconnect.
Restart the session, confirm output from the dead session is not presented as live, then attempt one command in an untrusted workspace and record the closed failure.
Close the product and confirm from the host that no descendant process remains.

external_oracles.description: A host inspection of the spawned child's environment shows no denied or secret-shaped variable, and the allow-listed names present match the declared policy.
A host process listing shows the child's image path equal to the configured workspace shell profile rather than the platform default.
The host-observed exit status and working directory for each command equal the values the product reported, including the OSC-derived directory.
A host read of the OS clipboard equals the terminal text that was selected, with no metadata appended.
After the product is closed a host process listing shows no descendant of the recorded product process id still running.

recovery_cases.description: A child killed from the host produces a truthful crashed or exited state with the real status, and the session offers restart or reconnect rather than appearing alive.
After a session is lost, output from the dead session is suppressed or marked stale and is never presented as live.
A command in an untrusted workspace fails closed with a visible reason and no child process is spawned, confirmed by the host process listing.
Output beyond the configured scrollback bound is dropped from the oldest end with the bound stated, rather than growing without limit or truncating silently.
If a declared shell for this platform is not installed, that shell's leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the child process ids and image paths, launch and exit timestamps, exit statuses, the parsed OSC metadata and a bounded transcript tail. The spawned process environment is recorded as allow-listed variable names only, never as values, and any token-shaped string is rejected before retention. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the Legion repository into a disposable directory, add a second worktree from a host shell, configure a local bare repository as the only remote, and record `git status --porcelain`, `git worktree list` and `git remote -v`.
Start a host per-process network capture filtered to the product process tree, then launch the packaged product on the clone.
Compare the source-control surface against the recorded host status: dirty paths, untracked paths, staged versus unstaged, branch and remote labels.
Edit a file, open its file diff and then a hunk-level diff, and compare both against host `git diff` output for the same path.
Stage one hunk, commit with an explicit message, and confirm the new commit against host `git log -1 --stat`.
Attempt a fetch, then a pull, then a push against the configured remote, recording the policy decision the product displays before each including the host and credential authorization state.
Revoke the remote's authorization in the product policy and attempt a push again; record the denial and confirm from the host that the bare repository received nothing.

Confirm the manual and agent worktrees added in step 1 appear in the source-control surface with their branches, then remove one through the product and confirm from the host that only that worktree is gone.
Create a checkpoint, make two further edits in different files, restore the checkpoint, and confirm from the host that the non-conflicting later edit outside the checkpoint scope survived.
Browse local history for one file, restore an earlier revision through the review surface, and compare the restored bytes with the recorded revision.
Make the worktree read-only from the host and attempt one checkpoint restore; record the fail-closed result and confirm the last known good file is intact.

external_oracles.description: Host `git status --porcelain`, `git diff` and `git diff --cached` output equals what the source-control surface displayed at the same moment, path for path and hunk for hunk.
Host `git log -1 --stat` reports the commit id, message and file list the product claimed to create.
A host inspection of the bare repository's refs and objects shows nothing was received during the denied push, and the network capture shows no connection the user did not explicitly authorize.
Host `git worktree list` before and after shows exactly the worktree the product removed and no other.
Host SHA-256 values after the checkpoint restore show the checkpointed files reverted and the non-conflicting later edit preserved.

recovery_cases.description: A remote operation without host or credential authorization is denied with a visible policy reason and produces no network attempt in the capture.
Any connection in the capture that the user did not explicitly authorize fails the run and is recorded as a defect.
Removing one worktree leaves every other worktree, its branch and its dirty files intact, verified from the host.
A checkpoint restore whose target changed on disk after the checkpoint was taken is refused or resolved explicitly, and the current work is preserved.
With the worktree read-only the restore fails closed with the exact OS error, the last known good file remains, and a retry is still possible.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture git status, log, index and worktree listings, the checkpoint and local-history metadata, and the network capture as connection metadata only with payloads discarded at capture time. Author identity is reduced to the configured test identity. The only remote is a local bare repository; no remote URL, credential helper output or token is captured. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the sample repository into a disposable directory on a dedicated volume whose free space can be constrained from the host, and record the SHA-256 of every file the run will touch.
Launch the packaged product, open three files, and make an edit in each.
Fill the volume from the host so the next write cannot complete, then save all three buffers.
Record the per-file result the product reports and confirm from the host that each file holds either its complete pre-edit content or its complete post-edit content, never a truncated mixture.
Confirm the buffers whose writes were denied are still dirty and recoverable, and that the failure names the storage condition.
Free the space, retry the save from the product, and confirm the bytes on disk now match the buffers.
Remove write permission from one file from the host, edit and save it, and record the permission failure and the retained on-disk bytes.
Restore permission, open a file whose declared encoding the product does not support, attempt an edit and a save, and record the unsupported-encoding report.
Kill the product process from the host while one buffer is dirty, relaunch, and record what recoverable text is offered and what the on-disk file contains.
Repeat one save after the restart, then read every touched file from the host and compare against the recorded hashes and the operations performed.

external_oracles.description: A host size and SHA-256 of every touched file after each failed save equals either the recorded pre-edit value or the complete post-edit value, and never a partial write.
A host read after each permission, storage and encoding failure shows the last known good file content unchanged.
A host read of the recovery store after the kill contains the dirty text that was offered for recovery, or its absence is recorded as the truthful loss the product reported.
The OS reports the original product process id absent and a new one after the kill, so the recovery is observed on a genuinely new process.

recovery_cases.description: A save that cannot complete for lack of space fails closed with the storage condition named, keeps the buffer dirty, and leaves the file recoverable.
A save denied by file permissions reports the exact OS error and leaves the on-disk bytes unchanged.
An unsupported or malformed encoding is reported rather than silently rewritten, and the file on disk is byte-identical afterwards.
After the process is killed the recoverable dirty text is offered, or its loss is reported truthfully; the on-disk file is still the pre-crash bytes either way.
Once the failing condition is removed the retry succeeds without a fabricated earlier success and without duplicating the edit.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the recorded file hashes before and after each step, the per-file save results, the OS error text and the recovery store listing. The workspace is a disposable clone on a dedicated volume. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on two different disposable workspaces in two windows and record each window's workspace identity, tab set, dock arrangement, font size and monitor placement.
Resize each window, then move one to a second display with a different scale factor, and confirm layout, font sizing and DPI scaling follow without losing tabs or focus.
Open a floating panel or secondary window, confirm it is tracked as part of the same workspace session, and record its placement.
Close both windows through the ordinary window close and relaunch, and confirm each restores its own workspace identity, tabs, docks and placement without borrowing the other's.
Use the native file-open dialog to open a file and the native save dialog to write one, and confirm from the host that the OS dialog was used and that the chosen paths were the ones written.
Copy from the editor and paste into another application, then copy from another application and paste into the editor, comparing both directions against the OS clipboard read from the host.
Commit an IME composition into the editor and confirm the committed text appears exactly once.

Store and then read a provider credential reference through the OS keyring path, confirm from the host keyring tool that an entry exists, and confirm from a host search that no secret value appears in any product-written file.

Start a terminal session and confirm from the host that the child is attached to a real PTY or ConPTY device, then change a workspace file from the host and confirm the filesystem watcher reports the external change.
Exercise the application menus and two OS-level keyboard shortcuts and record their effects.

Disable one platform facility from the host, for example the keyring service, repeat the dependent operation, and confirm the product reports the facility unavailable rather than substituting a fallback store.

external_oracles.description: A host UI-automation query or process listing shows the OS file dialog was the surface used, and the paths it returned are the paths the host finds written.
A host read of the OS clipboard equals the editor selection after a copy, and text placed on the clipboard by the host appears in the buffer after a paste.
A host keyring tool lists the stored entry by name, and a host search over every product-written file finds the secret value in none of them.
A host inspection shows the terminal child attached to a real PTY or ConPTY device rather than a pipe or a fixture.
A host read of each window's persisted session metadata names its own workspace, and neither file names the other window's tabs.

recovery_cases.description: With a platform facility disabled the dependent operation reports it unavailable with the exact facility named, and no headless or fixture substitute is used.
Removing the second display while a window is on it relocates the window to a visible display with its tabs and focus intact.
A display scale change is followed by layout and font sizing without clipped or unreachable controls; any regression is recorded as a defect.
One workspace restoring another workspace's tabs, docks or placement fails the run and is recorded as a defect.
An external change the watcher does not report is recorded by path as a missed notification rather than treated as absent.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the per-window session metadata, the window and monitor placement records, the dialog and clipboard comparisons, the keyring entry name and the PTY device identity. The keyring secret value is never read, captured or named; only the entry label is recorded. Clipboard content from other applications is limited to the synthetic string the run places there. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Record the reference hardware for this configuration, confirm it matches the ratified entry, and start a host resource sampler recording CPU, resident memory, open file descriptors or handles and thread count for the product process tree at a fixed interval.
Measure cold launch to first usable frame with a host clock or high-frame-rate capture, then close the product and measure warm launch the same way.
Open the ratified large workspace and measure input-to-paint for a keystroke, scroll latency over a long file, and the time from cancelling a running workspace search to the search actually stopping.
Measure terminal output throughput by running a command that emits a known number of lines and timing it from the host.
Work continuously for thirty minutes across editing, navigation, terminal, diagnostics, search and rendering, keeping the sampler running throughout.
Record the memory plateau, the peak CPU and the maximum descriptor, worker and thread counts reached during the window.
Cancel a long operation mid-flight and confirm the resources it held are released within the declared bound.
Induce a degraded condition, for example opening the 100 MB fixture, and confirm the product degrades visibly rather than stalling and that user work is preserved.
Close the product and confirm from the host that every child process, descriptor and temporary file it created is gone.
Compare every measured figure against the declared per-platform budget and record each as within budget, over budget or blocked.

external_oracles.description: The host resource sampler's series is the record of CPU, memory, descriptor, thread and worker counts; no figure is taken from the product's own report.
A host clock or high-frame-rate capture measures launch, input-to-paint, scroll and cancellation intervals independently of the product.
A host descriptor or handle listing before, during and after the window shows the count returning to its baseline after cancellation and close.
After close a host process listing and temporary-directory inventory match the recorded baseline, with no surviving child and no leftover temporary file.

recovery_cases.description: A measurement outside the declared budget is recorded as over budget with the measured figure; it is never re-run until favourable or averaged away.
If the ratified reference hardware is unavailable, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing hardware and never as passed on a substitute machine.
A cancelled operation whose resources are not released within the declared bound is recorded as a defect with the host sampler series as evidence.
A degraded condition that stalls the product instead of degrading visibly fails the run, and any user work lost is recorded.
Any child process, descriptor or temporary file surviving the close is recorded as a leak with its identity.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the host resource sampler series, the timing measurements, the reference hardware identity and the process and temporary-file inventories. Machine identifiers are reduced to a run-local pseudonym. The workspace is a disposable clone; no personal file is opened during the thirty-minute window. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start the platform accessibility provider on the target host, confirm from the host that it is running, and launch the packaged product on the disposable clone.
Enumerate every accessibility setting the product exposes, recording its name, its default value and where it is reachable.
For each setting in turn, change it and record the observable difference: the accessibility tree, the focus indicator, the rendered contrast or scale, or the announced text.
Relaunch the product and confirm each changed setting and its observable effect survive the restart.
Reset every setting to its default and confirm the observable effects return to the recorded defaults.
Read the settings file from the host and confirm the values there match what the product reported at each stage.
With the most restrictive combination of settings enabled, perform one keyboard-only journey: open a file, type a line, and save it.
Read the saved file from the host to confirm the journey completed under those settings.
Record by name any accessibility setting the product documents but does not expose, and any exposed setting with no observable effect.

external_oracles.description: A host accessibility tree dump taken before and after each setting change differs in the way that setting describes; a setting whose dump is unchanged is recorded as having no observable effect.
A host read of the settings file shows each changed value and, after the reset, each default value.
A host read of the file saved during the keyboard-only journey shows the typed line.
A host process listing shows the accessibility provider running for the whole window of the run.

recovery_cases.description: A setting whose change produces no observable difference in the tree, the rendering or the announcement is recorded by name as a defect.
A documented accessibility setting absent from the packaged build is recorded by name as failed and never omitted from the inventory.
If the accessibility provider cannot be started, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed or skipped.
A reset that leaves any setting or its observable effect away from the recorded default is recorded as a defect.
A setting that does not survive the restart is recorded by name with its lost value rather than re-applied before the check.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the accessibility setting inventory, the tree dumps for the Legion window subtree only, the settings file and the saved journey file. No screen reader speech log covering other applications is retained and no OS-wide accessibility recording is enabled. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, open the Canvas from the activity rail control, and record the Canvas arrangement metadata file path from the host.
Confirm every open file appears as a card carrying its own text and that the card names match the open tabs.
Drag one card with the pointer to a new position and move a second card using only the keyboard; confirm both moves update the arrangement and keep the moved card visible.
Create a connection between two distinct cards through their ports, then attempt a self-connection and an incomplete source-to-nothing drag, recording both refusals.
Inspect the created edge, confirm it is recorded as a person-drawn claim carrying its own type, then remove it and confirm the removal.

Add a new file node and a terminal node through the Canvas add controls, and confirm each was created through the owning workspace or terminal authority, with the terminal node backed by a real session.
Activate a file card, confirm it navigates to and focuses that buffer in the editor without creating a second editable copy, then edit the buffer and confirm the card text follows.

Enumerate the promised spatial node kinds present for the current working set - file, test, terminal, proposal and Assist suggestion - and record by name any promised kind that is absent or carries no status or action affordance.
Traverse cards, ports and the Canvas surface with the keyboard and capture a platform accessibility dump showing a distinct name for each.
Exercise one workflow action offered on a proposal, test or terminal node, confirm the result is produced by that node's owning authority, and record the lifecycle states shown.
Close and relaunch the product, confirm the arrangement, the connection set and the added nodes are restored, and compare the Canvas metadata read from the host before and after.

external_oracles.description: A host read of the persisted Canvas metadata records the node positions, the person-drawn edges and the added nodes, and matches the arrangement after the relaunch.
A host read of the file edited through the activated card shows the edit applied exactly once, proving the card did not create a second editor authority.
A platform accessibility dump reports a distinct name for the Canvas surface, each card and each port reached in the keyboard traversal.
The terminal node's child process id is visible to the host while it runs, and the workflow action exercised on a node produces an effect the host can observe outside the product.

recovery_cases.description: A self-connection is refused visibly and no edge is recorded in the persisted metadata.
A connection gesture released without a target is refused visibly and leaves the previous edge set unchanged.
A promised node kind that is absent, or present without truthful status and action affordances, is recorded by name as a failed outcome rather than omitted.
An arrangement, edge set or added node that does not survive the relaunch is recorded field by field against the persisted metadata.
Move OS focus away mid-drag and back; the arrangement is unchanged and the next keyboard move applies to the same node.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the persisted Canvas metadata, the accessibility dump filtered to the Legion window subtree, the card and edge inventory and the observed node action effects. Window captures are reviewed for incidental on-screen content before retention. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone with the ratified local provider route selected, and record the mutation-route inventory the product publishes together with the stated activation state of each route.
Record the SHA-256 of every file the run will touch and start a host per-process network capture filtered to the product process tree.

Request a change that produces a multi-file proposal and walk it through its lifecycle, recording the state the product reports at each transition and confirming no transition reached applied without passing validation and approval.
Attempt to approve a second proposal whose target file was changed from the host after the preview; record the stale denial and confirm from the host that no byte changed.

Submit a proposal naming a target outside the authorized workspace, one with an unsupported payload type, one whose target coverage is incomplete, and one replayed twice; record the deny-before-mutation result for each.

Create a batch proposal mixing a reversible and an irreversible operation; record the preflight result for every target, the declared atomic or best-effort behavior, the dry-run output, and the refusal of the unsupported mixture.
Apply a reversible batch and then roll it back, confirming from the host that every target returned to its recorded pre-apply hash and that any dirty buffer survived.

Read the audit ledger through the product's own query surface and from the host store, confirming each apply and rollback has a record with nonzero correlation, causality and event-sequence values and containing no source text, prompt or provider payload.

Confirm the trust surface projects the proposal ledger, the context and privacy scope, permission, risk, budget, rollback, selected route and egress decision, and that approval and denial are explicit intents reachable from the keyboard.

Turn on the opt-in auto-approval policy, record the deterministic rule ids it cites for a low-risk proposal, then submit a medium-risk change and confirm it pauses with a stated reason instead of auto-approving.
Confirm the risk classifier output is presented as advisory and that the apply still required both the policy decision and the human approval.
Confirm each denied future surface named in the mutation-route inventory is still visibly denied when invoked, and that a capability the selected route does not declare is refused at activation time.

Accept an agent-suggested terminal command through the command-proposal route, confirm the policy scope it declares, and compare the resulting child process and its bounded, redacted output with the host observation.
With Manual mode selected, attempt a hosted-route action and confirm it is denied locally with no entry in the network capture and no fallback.
Make the audit sink unwritable from the host and attempt an apply; confirm the apply fails closed and that no file changed.

external_oracles.description: Host SHA-256 values of every target file after each denial, apply and rollback equal the values the recorded lifecycle state implies, and nothing changed on any denial.

A host read of the audit store shows a paired record for every apply and rollback with nonzero correlation, causality and event-sequence values, and a byte search finds no source text, prompt, secret or provider payload in them.
The host per-process capture attributed to the product process tree shows no external connection during the Manual-mode denial and none for any route the run did not explicitly authorize.
A host process listing shows the approved terminal command's child running under the product process and absent after it exits, with the exit status matching what the product reported.

recovery_cases.description: A proposal whose target changed after preview is denied before mutation with a visible stale reason, and the external change survives intact.
A target outside the authorized workspace, an unsupported payload, an incomplete target set and a duplicate submission are each denied before mutation with a visible reason.
A partial batch failure preserves every dirty buffer, leaves metadata-only recovery state, and reports which targets applied and which did not.
With the audit sink unwritable the apply fails closed and no file changes; an apply that succeeds without its audit record fails the run.
Cancelling a proposal withdraws it, leaves every target byte-identical, and leaves the trust surface usable.
If the ratified local route cannot be started on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the mutation-route inventory, the recorded lifecycle states, the audit records, the file hashes and the network capture. Audit records are metadata only and are inspected before retention to confirm they carry no source text, prompt, completion, secret or provider payload. The network capture is retained as connection metadata with packet payloads discarded at capture time. No prompt or completion text is retained. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start from a clean product profile on the disposable clone with a host per-process network capture running, and record every tracked configuration file the product will write.

Complete first run and enumerate every provider and model the setup surface offers, recording provider kind, endpoint, model and whether each is local, self-hosted or hosted, together with any unavailable prerequisite it states.

Configure the ratified local runtime in managed mode, then switch it to explicit external-runtime mode pointing at a runtime the host started; record which process the product reports it supervises and confirm from the host process listing which process it actually owns.

Stop and start the managed runtime from the product, recording the bounded start, stop and health transitions, and confirm from the host that the runtime process was granted no workspace path beyond its declared scope.
Add a hosted provider credential, replace it, revoke it and delete it, recording the state the product reports after each step.

Search every tracked configuration file, projection dump, event log, diagnostic and support bundle from the host for the credential value, confirm it appears in none of them, and confirm the OS-backed reference exists instead.

Validate the endpoint, model and declared capabilities before activation, record the named health, latency, locality and availability state for the selected route, then point the endpoint at an unreachable address and record the failure state.
Query capabilities per provider and confirm an action requiring a capability the selected route does not declare is refused at activation time rather than at invocation.
With workspace consent withheld, attempt a hosted call and confirm it is refused and that the capture shows no connection.
Grant explicit egress consent, record the route, context, retention and budget the product displays and the preflight token and cost estimate, and let one hosted call complete.
Compare the reconciled usage, cache, latency, cost and egress metadata the product reports against what the network capture observed for that request.
Set a budget ceiling below the next request's estimate and confirm the request is refused before dispatch.
Select Manual mode and repeat the hosted action, confirming a local denial with no fallback and no entry in the capture.

external_oracles.description: The host per-process capture is the record of every connection the product made: none while consent was withheld or Manual mode was selected, and exactly one for the consented hosted call.
A host search for the credential value across every product-written configuration file, log, diagnostic and support bundle returns no match at any point in the run.
A host keyring tool shows the credential reference created, replaced and then removed, matching the lifecycle the product reported.
The request and response sizes and timing the capture observed agree with the usage, latency and egress metadata the product reconciled after the call.
A host process listing distinguishes the managed runtime the product supervises from the externally started runtime, matching the mode the product reported in each case.

recovery_cases.description: With consent withheld the hosted action is refused locally with a visible reason and produces no connection in the capture.
An unreachable endpoint produces a truthful unavailable health state and never a fabricated success or a silently substituted route.
A request whose preflight estimate exceeds the ceiling is refused before dispatch, with no connection in the capture.
After revocation the route reports unavailable, the OS-backed reference is gone, and no cached secret allows a further call.
If no hosted credential is available for this configuration, the hosted leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing credential; a recorded fixture is never substituted for a live hosted route.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The credential used is a run-scoped test credential that is revoked at the end of the run; its value is never captured, copied, quoted or named, and the host search for it records only whether a match was found. Capture the provider and model inventory, the reported health and usage metadata, the keyring entry labels and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Prepare a disposable workspace containing a source tree, an ignored directory, a generated file, a binary file, an oversized file, a symlink pointing outside the workspace and a file carrying a synthetic secret-shaped token; record every path and hash from the host.
Launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected and a host per-process network capture running, and let the workspace index build to its reported ready state.

Open two files, leave one dirty, select a range, run one terminal command and make one Git change so that files, buffers, symbols, diagnostics, terminal excerpts and diff are all available, then start an action that assembles a context manifest.

Open the context inspector before dispatch and record every selected item with its source identity, content fingerprint, freshness, inclusion reason, privacy class and redaction outcome, together with the provider and model route, the budget and the egress state.

Confirm the ignored, generated, binary, oversized, symlink-escaped and secret-bearing sources are excluded or redacted with a visible reason, then exclude one further item by hand and confirm it leaves the selection.
Record the planned manifest as a structured document rather than a freeform prompt, dispatch the request, then record the actual manifest and compare the two.
Compare what the network capture observed leaving the machine against the reviewed manifest minus the redacted items, and confirm there is no other delta.

Enable memory context, confirm it is opt-in and carries workspace, user and source identity with retention state, review one memory record, exclude it, and confirm it is absent from the next manifest.

Ask for a retrieval-backed answer and confirm the returned symbols, references, imports, exports and chunks carry source identity and provenance and are bounded by the declared ranking limit, with any vector or model-backed retrieval explicitly qualified.
Edit one included file from the host after the manifest is reviewed but before the next dispatch, and confirm the changed context fails stale before egress rather than being sent.
Lower the token or byte budget below the assembled size and confirm the truncation and the exclusions are explained deterministically.

Restart the product, rebuild the index, and replay the recorded manifest from its metadata, fingerprints and citations, confirming the replay reproduces the same selection without any retained raw source.

external_oracles.description: The bytes the host capture observed for the dispatched request equal the reviewed manifest minus the redacted items, with no other delta.
The synthetic secret token and the content of the symlink target outside the workspace appear nowhere in the capture and in no product-written file.
Every content fingerprint the manifest records equals the host-computed hash of that file at the moment of selection.
The replayed manifest names the same items with the same fingerprints and citations as the recorded one, reconstructed without any retained raw source.

recovery_cases.description: Context changed after review fails stale before egress; a request dispatched with silently refreshed context fails the run.
A budget below the assembled size produces a deterministic truncation with the excluded items named, not an arbitrary or silent drop.
After restart and index rebuild the freshness state is truthful; stale entries are marked rather than presented as current.
An excluded or revoked memory record cannot reappear in a later manifest; if it does, the run fails and the record is reported.

If the host per-process capture cannot attribute traffic to the product process tree, the egress-equality part of the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite; the product's own report never substitutes for it.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The workspace is synthetic and the secret token is generated for the run. Capture the manifest metadata, fingerprints, citations, inclusion reasons and redaction outcomes; raw source content is not retained, and the capture is kept as connection metadata plus payload sizes and hashes with packet payloads discarded at capture time. Any evidence found to contain the synthetic secret token is destroyed and the run recorded as failed. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone one real multi-file repository per supported language group - Rust, TypeScript or JavaScript, and Python - into disposable directories, record every file hash, and launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected and a host per-process network capture running.

Type in a source file, confirm inline completion or ghost text appears from the selected route, accept one suggestion, and confirm the acceptance produced a proposal rather than a direct buffer mutation.

Ask the assistant rail to explain a selected symbol and confirm the answer names the provider, the model and the context items it used through the projection controls; confirm each rail command is a tracked capability with a visible permission state.

Request an inline edit at an anchored position, confirm the produced proposal preserves the anchor and the buffer version, then edit the file from the host and confirm the next apply fails visibly as stale rather than applying to moved text.
Request a change spanning at least five files, confirm one reviewable proposal set is produced with complete target and version coverage, and confirm from the host that no file has been written yet.

Start a long request, watch the streamed progress, confirm each streamed code block offers an apply-as-proposal affordance, cancel the request mid-stream, and confirm nothing from the cancelled output is applied.
Retry the request, then in the review surface accept some hunks, reject others, edit one hunk in place, and apply, performing every one of those actions from the keyboard only.
Confirm the evidence panel shows structured fields rather than a freeform text dump.
Read every affected file from the host, compare against the review decisions, and confirm a checkpoint entry exists for the apply.
Undo the apply and confirm from the host that every file returned to its recorded pre-apply hash.

Kill the provider process or block its endpoint mid-request, confirm the loss is reported and no partial output is applied, then restart the product mid-session and confirm the session state and the user's own edits survive.
Repeat the representative task once per language group, and once against the hosted route if a credential is available, recording the outcome and every recovery result for each.
Read the telemetry the run produced from the host and confirm it is metadata-only unless the richer opt-in was enabled.

external_oracles.description: Host SHA-256 values show no file written before approval, exactly the accepted hunks written after apply, and every file back at its pre-apply hash after undo.
A host read of the checkpoint store shows an entry for the apply naming the affected files and the proposal it came from.
The host per-process capture shows a connection only for the routes the run explicitly authorized, and none after a cancellation or a provider loss.
Every review action in step 7 is recorded as performed without pointer input, and each one has an effect the host can read on disk or in the checkpoint store.

recovery_cases.description: A cancelled request applies nothing; any file changed after a cancellation fails the run.
An inline edit whose anchor or buffer version moved is refused visibly and never applied to relocated text.
Provider loss mid-request is reported truthfully, no partial output is applied, and the user's edits survive.
A conflicting external change before apply is reported and resolved explicitly, preserving both the external change and the user's dirty work.
Restarting mid-session preserves the user's edits and reports truthfully whether the assistant session itself survived.
If no hosted credential is available, the hosted leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing credential and never as passed on the local route.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. Capture the proposal diffs, the review decisions, the checkpoint entries, the file hashes and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. No prompt or completion text is retained beyond the proposal diff itself, and provider payloads are recorded as metadata only. The repositories are disposable clones. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the sample repository into a disposable directory, record every file hash, and launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected.
Apply a multi-file change through the proposal route and confirm a checkpoint entry was created for the apply, recording its identifier.
Apply a batch change and confirm a second checkpoint entry exists for it.
Make one manual edit in a file the apply did not touch, and a second manual edit in a file it did touch but in a region it did not change.
Restore the first checkpoint through the ordinary product control, recording how that control was reached.
Read every file from the host and confirm the applied change was reverted while both manual edits survived.
Attempt to restore a checkpoint whose target file was changed from the host after the checkpoint was taken, and record the conflict handling.
Query the audit ledger through the product surface and from the host store, confirming every checkpoint creation and restore appears with its identifier and timestamps.
Restart the product and confirm the checkpoint list and the restored state survive.

external_oracles.description: Host SHA-256 values after the restore show the applied change reverted and every untouched file unchanged.
A host read shows both non-conflicting manual edits still present after the restore; losing either fails the run.
A host read of the audit store contains a record for every checkpoint creation and restore, with identifiers matching what the product's query surface returned.
After restart the checkpoint list read from the host store is unchanged and the restored file bytes are still in place.

recovery_cases.description: A restore whose target changed on disk after the checkpoint is refused or resolved explicitly; it never silently overwrites the external change.
A checkpoint whose stored content is missing or fails its integrity check is reported and the restore is refused.
With the checkpoint store unwritable the apply reports the failure, and an apply that proceeds without a checkpoint fails the run.
Restarting after a restore preserves the restored bytes and the checkpoint list.
If restore is reachable only through a developer or hidden command rather than an ordinary product control, the run is failed and the missing control is named.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Capture the checkpoint identifiers, the audit records, the file hashes before and after each apply and restore, and the path by which the restore control was reached. Audit records are metadata only. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the Legion repository into a disposable directory, record every file hash and `git worktree list`, and launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected.

Author a delegated task with an explicit structured scope, an ordered plan with named targets, the selected route, a budget and an approval policy; edit the plan before starting and confirm the edited plan is what runs.
Start the worker and record from the host the disposable worktree or copy it created, its path, and the sandbox the product reports as active together with the platform caveats it names for this OS.
Watch the tool turns and record each read, edit and project-command call together with its audit row, confirming each row carries the same causality id as its call.
While the worker runs, compare the main workspace hashes with the recorded values and confirm the worker's writes land only inside the disposable scope.

Feed the frozen malformed tool-call corpus into the worker and confirm every vector is either recovered exactly or refused with a structured diagnostic returned to the model, counted against the retry budget, audited as malformed, and never dispatched; confirm no truncated or adversarial input causes a crash.

Submit an edit-as-proposal fragment that matches zero locations and one that matches several, and confirm each is refused with a diagnostic naming the nearest line, that whitespace and line-ending drift does not match, that the refusal is retryable within the run, and that no file was written.
Request a path outside the declared scope and confirm the tool call is refused at call time by the structured scope rather than after the fact.
Let the worker run the real project command and compare its recorded exit status and output fingerprint with the same command run by a host shell.
Confirm the produced proposal is complete, carries target versions and the verification evidence, and offers per-hunk review, and confirm from the host that no file changed before approval.
Approve the proposal, read every affected file from the host, and confirm the change matches the review.
Confirm the tool output presented to the model was bounded and that secret-shaped strings and large blobs were redacted before reaching it.
Inspect the delegate projection and confirm the task, scope, plan, budget, worker, sandbox, evidence and review controls all report truthful lifecycle states.

external_oracles.description: Host hashes of the main workspace are unchanged for the whole run until the proposal is approved, while the disposable worktree shows the worker's writes.
A host read of the audit store shows one row per tool call with a matching causality id, including a row for every refused malformed or out-of-scope call.
A host shell running the same project command reproduces the exit status and the output fingerprint the worker recorded.
Host reads after approval show exactly the reviewed change in exactly the reviewed files.
A host read of what was presented to the model shows it within the declared bound and containing no secret-shaped string or large blob.

recovery_cases.description: A malformed tool call cannot be dispatched; the diagnostic is returned to the model, counted against the retry budget and audited, and a transport-shape failure remains a hard provider error.
An out-of-scope path or command fails closed at call time, is audited, and leaves the main workspace untouched.
A fragment matching zero or several locations is refused with the nearest line named, is retryable, and never writes the file.
Exhausting a time, token, tool, output or process budget stops the worker with a truthful exhaustion state and no partial proposal presented as complete.
If the ratified local route cannot be started, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the task definition, the plan revisions, the tool-call and audit rows, the worktree inventory, the project command output fingerprint and the file hashes. Model-visible tool output is retained bounded and is scanned for secret-shaped strings before retention; any match is removed and recorded as a redaction. No prompt or completion text is retained beyond the proposal diff. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the Legion repository into a disposable directory, record every file hash, the host process listing and the temporary-directory inventory, start a host per-process network capture, and launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected.
Start a delegated task and confirm from the product surface which sandbox is active and which platform-specific caveats apply on this OS.
Run each escape-attempt fixture in turn: a write outside the declared scope, a read of a forbidden path, a network egress attempt without permission, and a command outside the allowed set.
For each attempt, confirm the operation failed closed, that an audit row records it, and that nothing outside the disposable scope changed on the host.
Confirm every worker write landed inside the disposable worktree and that the main workspace was never the direct target of any tool call.
Cancel a running worker gracefully and confirm it stops accepting tool calls, reports cancelled, and has its worktree, lease and sandbox reaped.
Start another worker and hard-kill it from the host; confirm the product reports the loss, reaps the child processes, and cleans the worktree, lease and sandbox.
Restart the product with a worker interrupted and confirm the recovery state offered, and that the task definition and the evidence collected so far survive.
Confirm each declared worker state has an explicit affordance in the product surface and that recovering from each is possible from that surface.

Repeat the task once per supported language group and, if a hosted credential is available, once on the hosted route, recording denial, budget, conflict, cancellation, provider-loss, crash, restart and cleanup outcomes for each.
Close the product and compare the host process listing and the temporary-directory inventory with the recorded baseline.

external_oracles.description: After close the host process listing and temporary-directory inventory match the recorded baseline, with no surviving worker, sandbox or worktree.
A host read of the audit store contains a row for every escape attempt with its refusal reason.
Host hashes of the main workspace are unchanged across every escape attempt, cancellation and kill.
The host per-process capture shows no connection for the unpermitted egress attempt.

recovery_cases.description: After a graceful cancellation the worker accepts no further tool call and its worktree, lease and sandbox are reaped.
A hard kill from the host leaves no orphan child, worktree or sandbox, and the product reports the loss truthfully.
Restarting after an interrupted worker offers a truthful recovery state and preserves the task definition and collected evidence.
A platform where the sandbox cannot enforce a declared boundary is recorded blocked with the exact caveat and never as passed.
If no hosted credential is available, the hosted leg is recorded blocked with the exact missing credential.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the sandbox identity and its caveats, the escape-attempt fixtures and their refusals, the audit rows, the process and temporary-directory inventories, and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. The escape fixtures target only synthetic paths created for the run. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Clone the Legion repository into a disposable directory, record every file hash and the host process listing, and launch the packaged product with the ratified local route selected.
Author a multi-worker plan of at least three tasks with one dependency, editing the plan before approval, and confirm the workflow refuses to start from unedited opaque instruction text.
Confirm each plan revision produced an audit row and a diffable representation, that approving the plan produced a DAG with stable node ids, and that a rejected plan produced no DAG.
Start the run and confirm from the host process listing that the two independent workers were alive at the same instant as real worker processes, with no mock worker in the product path.
Confirm the dependent task started only after its prerequisite completed, then deliberately fail a prerequisite and confirm its dependents are blocked rather than started.
Confirm each worker ran in its own disposable worktree under its declared scope and tool permissions, and that the main workspace hashes were unchanged during the run.
Set aggregate and per-worker time, token, tool, output and process budgets, exhaust one, and confirm the exhaustion outcome is truthful and visible in the command centre.

Arrange two workers to edit overlapping regions and confirm the conflict is detected, that affected dependents pause, that a human-resolution affordance appears, and that a reviewable conflict-resolution proposal is produced.
Confirm every worker output is proposal-mediated and that the merge-readiness report cites the verification evidence per branch or task before any per-hunk approval.
Grant and then revoke a permission for one worker, stop a second worker gracefully and hard-kill a third, and confirm no further unauthorized call occurs after each.
Cancel the fleet mid-run, restart the product, and confirm the run resumes deterministically without replaying completed workers or duplicating their effects.

Inspect the command centre and confirm every column and field is sourced from the coordinator projection rather than hand-edited state, that each stream tag is rendered explicitly, and that plan, dependency, worker, scope, budget, evidence, permission, conflict and recovery state are all truthful.
Approve the final merge, read every affected file from the host, and compare against the reviewed proposals.
Close the product and confirm from the host that no worker process, worktree or sandbox leaked.

external_oracles.description: A host process listing sampled during the run shows two independent worker processes alive at the same instant, each a child of the product.
Host hashes of the main workspace are unchanged for the whole run until the final merge is approved, while each worker's worktree shows only its own writes.
Host reads after the merge show exactly the reviewed changes in exactly the reviewed files.
After the cancel and resume, host hashes show each completed worker's change applied exactly once.
After close the host process listing and worktree inventory match the recorded baseline.

recovery_cases.description: A failed or conflicted prerequisite blocks its dependents with a truthful state; a dependent that starts anyway fails the run.
Overlapping worker edits pause the affected dependents and produce a reviewable proposal instead of a silent last-writer-wins merge.
An exhausted aggregate or per-worker budget stops the affected work with the exhaustion named and no partial result presented as complete.
After a permission is revoked or a worker is stopped or killed, no further call from it succeeds, verified from the audit rows and the host process listing.
Resuming after cancellation or restart replays no completed worker and duplicates no effect; any duplication fails the run.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the plan revisions and their diffs, the DAG node ids, the coordinator projection, the audit rows, the merge-readiness report, the worker process and worktree inventories and the file hashes. Model-visible content is bounded and scanned for secret-shaped strings before retention. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Start the named supported external MCP server, the named supported external MCP client and the named supported external ACP agent on the host over the ratified transports, and record each peer's implementation name, version and process id.
Launch the packaged product on a disposable clone with a host per-process network capture running, and record every file hash.

Connect to the external MCP server as a client, complete the authenticated handshake, and record the negotiated peer identity, protocol version, credentials used and the discovered tools, resources and prompts.
Invoke one tool, read one resource and use one prompt, confirming the results are bounded and redacted by policy and that no workspace file was mutated directly by the peer.
Send a malformed frame from the peer, return an oversized result, and force a request timeout; record the handling of each and confirm no partial result is presented as complete.
Revoke the peer's permission mid-session and confirm no further call succeeds, then kill the peer process and confirm the reconnect behavior and the audit rows written.

Expose Legion's MCP server role to the named external MCP client over a ratified transport, authenticate the peer and its credentials, and complete capability discovery and a bounded tool, resource and prompt exchange.

Confirm every change the external client requests arrives as a Legion proposal requiring approval rather than a direct write, then repeat the malformed, oversized, timeout, process-death, cancellation, reconnect, revocation and clean-disconnect cases against the server role.

Connect the external ACP agent as a host, negotiate peer identity, version and capabilities, apply the credential and privacy policy, hand it a scoped task with context, and watch the streamed progress.
Confirm every external edit returned became a Legion proposal and every external log line became an evidence row, then approve the proposal and compare the affected files against a host read.

Confirm both peer kinds run under the same containment by attempting one out-of-scope path, one disallowed command, one unbudgeted call and one unauthorized network destination from each, recording the denial for every case.
Run one multi-worker cross-file task that uses both peers, exercise a conflict and its approval, interrupt and recover the run, and record the external verification of the result.
Close the product and confirm from the host that no peer child process, sandbox or temporary directory leaked.

external_oracles.description: A host process listing and the peer's own log confirm the implementation name and version the product reported for each negotiated session.
Host hashes show no workspace file changed until a Legion proposal was approved, for both the MCP server role and the ACP agent.
After close the host process listing and temporary-directory inventory match the recorded baseline, with no peer child surviving.
A host read of the audit store contains a row for every peer invocation, denial, revocation, disconnect and reconnect, with the peer identity recorded.
The host per-process capture shows connections only to the ratified peer endpoints and none for the unauthorized destination attempt.

recovery_cases.description: A malformed or error frame is rejected with a visible diagnostic, is audited, and causes no mutation and no fabricated result.
A peer process that dies is reported unavailable, its in-flight work is not presented as complete, and reconnect is explicit.
After revocation no further peer call succeeds, verified from the audit rows and from the peer's own log.
A request that exceeds its deadline is cancelled, reported as timed out, and leaves no partial effect.
If a named peer implementation cannot be obtained for this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with its exact name and version and never as passed against a substitute.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the negotiated peer identities and versions, the capability inventories, the bounded exchange results, the audit rows and the network capture as connection metadata with payloads discarded at capture time. Peer credentials are run-scoped and are revoked at the end of the run; their values are never captured or named. Exchange payloads are inspected for secret-shaped strings and raw source before retention. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Build the ratified signed WASM extension and the hostile fixture modules from their sources on the host, record each artifact's SHA-256 and signature, and confirm the WIT files compile and the host bindings are generated.
Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone, record every file hash, the host process listing and the extension directory inventory, and open the extension surface.
Install the signed bundled grammar and theme extension through the product UI, record the structured permission list presented at install, and accept it.

Confirm the extension's declared WIT contributions took effect in the product, that its activation events fired as declared, and that its host calls are answered through versioned bounded request and response envelopes within the declared quotas.
Enable and disable the extension and confirm the contributions appear and disappear accordingly, with cancellation of an in-flight host call handled explicitly.

Update the extension to a newer signed version, interrupt the update mid-way by terminating the product, relaunch, and confirm the rollback left a working previous version with its provenance inspectable.
Tamper with the artifact bytes from the host and attempt to install it; confirm the refusal happens before any module code runs, and repeat with an unsigned artifact.

Install and run each hostile fixture in turn - attempts at ambient filesystem, environment, process, network, terminal and direct storage access - and confirm each is contained and denied and that an audit row records the attempt.
Drive one fixture past its declared quota and confirm the ceiling is enforced rather than exceeded.
Force an extension crash and confirm it is quarantined without taking the product down, then restart the product and confirm the reactivation behavior for the quarantined extension.
Attempt a workspace change from an extension and confirm it arrives as a proposal requiring approval rather than a direct write.
Add a VSIX to the extension surface, confirm its metadata is reported, and confirm from the host process listing that no Node runtime or other interpreter process was started for it.
Remove the extension and compare the host file, process and extension directory inventory with the recorded baseline.

external_oracles.description: A host verifier confirms the signature on the accepted artifact and rejects the tampered and unsigned artifacts; its exact output is retained.
Host observation of the filesystem, process table and network capture shows no write, spawn or connection attributable to any hostile module.
Host hashes show no workspace file changed from an extension request until the resulting proposal was approved.
A host process listing during and after the VSIX metadata report shows no Node or other interpreter process started by the product.

recovery_cases.description: A tampered or unsigned artifact is refused before any module code runs; an install that proceeds fails the run and is recorded as a security defect.
An update interrupted mid-way rolls back to a working previous version whose hash the host can verify.
A crashing extension is quarantined with the product still running, and its reactivation state after restart is truthful.
A module driven past its declared quota is stopped at the ceiling with the quota named, not allowed to continue.

If the ratified signed extension artifact or its signing material cannot be produced for this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed on an unsigned substitute.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strict policy. Capture the artifact hashes, the verifier output, the permission lists presented at install, the audit rows for every contained attempt, the quota enforcement records and the directory and process inventories. No signing private key is captured or named; only the verifier's printed subject. The hostile fixtures operate only on synthetic paths created for the run. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.

steps: Build the restrictive enterprise policy bundle from the ratified source on the host, sign it with the run-scoped test signing key, and record its SHA-256, its declared ceilings and its expiry.
Launch the packaged product on the disposable clone with a host per-process network capture running, and record the effective policy the product reports before the bundle is applied.

Distribute the signed bundle through the configured enterprise policy path and confirm the product adopts it atomically, reporting the new effective identity, AI, extension, remote, collaboration, telemetry, retention and export ceilings.

For each ceiling in turn, attempt the action it forbids and record the denial: a hosted provider call above the AI ceiling, an extension install above the extension ceiling, a telemetry consent above the telemetry ceiling, and an export above the export ceiling.
Present a bundle signed by an untrusted key and then a bundle whose version is older than the installed one; confirm both are refused and that the current effective policy is unchanged.
Install an already-expired bundle, confirm the expiry behavior the product declares, then disconnect the policy source and confirm the offline cache behavior it declares.
Export the tenant-scoped audit records through the product's export control to a host path and inspect every byte of the export.
Confirm the export is metadata-safe - no editor text, prompt, provider payload, secret or unredacted absolute path - and that each record is externally verifiable against the audit store.
Apply the retention control to expire a subset, request deletion, record the deletion handle and receipt, and confirm from the host that the deleted records are gone and the retained ones intact.
Restart the product and confirm the effective policy, the retention state and the deletion receipts survive.

external_oracles.description: A host verifier confirms the signature and version of the accepted bundle and rejects the untrusted and downgrade bundles; its exact output is retained.
Each forbidden action produced no effect the host can observe: no connection in the capture, no installed artifact, no written export and no consent state change.
A host byte-level inspection of the export finds no editor text, prompt, provider payload, secret-shaped string or unredacted absolute path.
After deletion a host listing shows the expired records absent and the retained records intact, with the receipt identifier matching what the product displayed.

recovery_cases.description: A bundle signed by an untrusted key is refused and the previously effective policy is unchanged; adoption of it fails the run as a security defect.
A bundle older than the installed one is refused with the version comparison stated.
An expired bundle and a disconnected policy source produce the declared expiry and offline-cache behavior; a silent fall back to unrestricted policy fails the run.
A failed deletion is reported with the retained data still accounted for and no receipt issued.
If no enterprise policy distribution path is available on this configuration, the run is recorded blocked with the exact missing prerequisite and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: Strictest policy. The signing key is run-scoped and is destroyed at the end of the run; no key material is captured or named. Capture the bundle hash and declared ceilings, the verifier output, the recorded denials, the export payload and the deletion receipts. The export is inspected byte by byte before retention; an export found to contain raw source, a prompt or a secret is destroyed and the run recorded as failed. Tenant identifiers are reduced to a run-local pseudonym. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate and honour the deletion receipt.

steps: Start from a clean product profile on the disposable clone with a host per-process network capture running and a host-controlled collection endpoint configured as the only destination; record the consent state files the product writes.
Confirm at first run that crash, product and raw-training consent are three separate controls and that every one of them is off by default.
Work for several minutes with all consent off and confirm from the capture, from the host endpoint log and from the spool directory that nothing was captured, queued or uploaded.
Turn product telemetry consent on, record the purpose, retention and destination the product displays, and confirm the enterprise ceiling in force is reflected in what the control allows.
Trigger an event and open the capture preview before upload, recording the exact scope, purpose, retention, destination, provenance and redaction result it shows.
Compare the payload the host endpoint received with the preview and confirm it is metadata-only, containing no editor text, prompt or source content.

Turn raw-training consent on, repeat the capture, and confirm the richer content appears only now, only within the previewed scope, and with redaction applied at the boundary before the payload leaves.
Take the host endpoint offline, generate further events, and confirm they queue in the recoverable local spool with a visible pending state and no data loss.
Corrupt the spool from the host, restart the product, and confirm the corrupt entries are reported and recovered or discarded without blocking new capture.

Confirm the key inventory and the escrow and rotation policy are recorded, and record any prerequisite missing any of those parts.
Confirm an external security audit or penetration test engagement is scheduled and that its report is archived, and verify the archived report's hash from the host.
Record every prerequisite and every cited archive that is absent, with the exact owner action needed to obtain it.

external_oracles.description: The host tree and history search output is the record that no signing secret is committed; absence is proven by the search rather than asserted.
Each cited archived artifact is resolved and hashed by the host, and the hash is compared with the one the ledger records.
The signer and verifier status of every release descriptor is read from the descriptor file itself.
Each named external prerequisite is matched to its checklist row, EXT-* mapping and owner action, and any missing part is recorded by name.

recovery_cases.description: Any committed signing secret fails the run immediately, is reported as a security defect, and its value is never quoted in the evidence.
A cited archive that does not resolve, or whose hash differs from the ledger, is recorded as a stale citation and never accepted.
An external prerequisite that is absent is recorded blocked with the exact owner action required, never as passed or skipped.
A ledger citation pointing at evidence from a different candidate revision is recorded as stale and not counted.
If no external security audit engagement is scheduled or no report is archived, the row is recorded blocked with the exact owner action and never as passed.

scenarios.sensitive_artifact_policy: No signing secret, private key, keychain entry, API key or credential is captured, copied or named beyond its checklist row label; the history search records only whether a match was found and where. Capture the descriptor statuses, the checklist inventory, the resolved archive paths and their hashes. Redact absolute user-home segments. Retain under the sealed run evidence directory for the candidate; delete with the candidate.
